Costa Rica BOLD Dashboard Components

Leaflet map, phylum treemap, BIN overlap (UpSet/chord), and iNEXT accumulation curves

Setup

Install any missing CRAN packages, then load all required libraries. BOLDNODE is not on CRAN and is assumed to already be installed.

Code 
cran_packages <- c(
  "BOLDconnectR",
  "dplyr",
  "leaflet",
  "tidyr",
  "ggplot2",
  "treemapify",
  "scales",
  "tibble",
  "circlize",
  "purrr",
  "iNEXT",
  "UpSetR" # Alternative source: devtools::install_github("hms-dbmi/UpSetR")
)

missing_packages <- cran_packages[!sapply(cran_packages, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing_packages)
}

invisible(lapply(cran_packages, library, character.only = TRUE))

# BOLDNODE is not installed from CRAN - assumed already available
library(BOLDNODE)

Load data

Using the latest data package from BOLD data packages.

Code 
parquet_path <- "/Users/sameerpadhye/Desktop/R data/Data/BOLD_Public.24-Jul-2026.parquet"
geography_filter <- "Costa Rica"

bold_data_search <- BOLDNODE::bold_parquet_search(
  parquet_path,
  geography = geography_filter
)
The search has 6967906 records in the dataset

1. Leaflet map of distinct coordinates

Code 
leaflet_data_search <- bold_data_search %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    coord_clean = sql("replace(replace(trim(coord), '[', ''), ']', '')"),
    # Instr here gives the position of the substring. Here it checks that the string contains a comma before splitting and casting as a double
    lat = sql(
      "CASE WHEN instr(replace(replace(trim(coord), '[', ''), ']', ''), ',') > 0
        THEN CAST(split_part(replace(replace(trim(coord), '[', ''), ']', ''), ',', 1) AS DOUBLE)
        ELSE NULL END"
    ),
    lon = sql(
      "CASE WHEN instr(replace(replace(trim(coord), '[', ''), ']', ''), ',') > 0
        THEN CAST(split_part(replace(replace(trim(coord), '[', ''), ']', ''), ',', 2) AS DOUBLE)
        ELSE NULL END"
    )
  )

leaflet_data <- leaflet_data_search %>%
  filter(!is.na(coord)) %>%
  select(c(
    "country.ocean",
    "country_iso",
    "province.state",
    "region",
    "sector",
    "site_code",
    "coord",
    "lat",
    "lon"
  )) %>%
  distinct(coord, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  collect()

# Build the map
leaflet_map <- leaflet(data = leaflet_data) %>%

  # Dark base map (better contrast for points)
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%

  # Points
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~lon,
    lat = ~lat,
    radius = 4,
    color = "white",
    weight = 1,
    fillColor = "orangered",
    fillOpacity = 0.8,
    popup = ~ paste0(
      "<b>Region:</b> ",
      region,
      "<br><b>Sector:</b> ",
      sector,
      "<br><b>Site code:</b> ",
      site_code,
      "<br><b>Coordinates:</b> ",
      coord
    )
  )

leaflet_map

2. Treemap of data based on phyla

Code 
# -----------------------------------
# Phylum summary
# -----------------------------------

phylum_treemap <- bold_data_search %>%
  filter(!is.na(bin_uri)) %>%
  group_by(phylum) %>%
  summarise(
    tot = n_distinct(sampleid),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    phylum_rank = row_number(desc(tot)),
    phylum_group = if_else(
      phylum_rank <= 5,
      phylum,
      "Others"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(phylum_group) %>%
  summarise(
    tot = sum(tot),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(tot)) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(
    # Log transformation so very large groups do not
    # completely dominate the treemap
    tot_scaled = log10(tot + 1)
  )
Warning: Missing values are always removed in SQL aggregation functions.
Use `na.rm = TRUE` to silence this warning
This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
Code 
# -----------------------------------
# Dynamic colour palette
# -----------------------------------

phylum_levels <- phylum_treemap %>%
  pull(phylum_group) %>%
  unique()

# Exclude "Others" from the main palette
main_phyla <- setdiff(
  phylum_levels,
  "Others"
)

# Generate as many contrasting colours as required
phylum_colors <- setNames(
  grDevices::hcl.colors(
    length(main_phyla),
    palette = "Dark 3"
  ),
  main_phyla
)

# Add a consistent colour for "Others"
if ("Others" %in% phylum_levels) {
  phylum_colors["Others"] <- "grey40"
}

# -----------------------------------
# Treemap
# -----------------------------------

phylum_treemap_plot <- ggplot(
  phylum_treemap,
  aes(
    area = tot_scaled,
    fill = phylum_group,
    label = paste0(
      phylum_group,
      "\n",
      scales::comma(tot)
    )
  )
) +
  geom_treemap(
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_treemap_text(
    colour = "white",
    place = "centre",
    grow = TRUE,
    reflow = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = phylum_colors
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Samples by phylum",
    fill = "Phylum"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    )
  )

3. BIN overlaps between ecoregions (UpSet plot)

Using an UpSet plot, BIN overlaps between the top 80% ecoregions by occurrences is visualized.

Code 
# Data for BIN overlaps
upset_df <- bold_data_search %>%
  filter(marker_code == "COI-5P") %>%
  filter(!is.na(biome)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(bin_uri)) %>%
  distinct(., .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  #filter(ecoregion%in%(ecoregions_top80%>%filter(cum_pct_occ<=90)%>%pull(ecoregion)))%>%
  group_by(biome, bin_uri) %>%
  summarise(total_occ = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  collect() %>%
  spread(key = biome, value = total_occ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ replace(., is.na(.), 0))) %>%
  column_to_rownames("bin_uri")

# The above data also gives the total number of intersections that can be used as an argument for the UpSet plot

# Create a list of species for each ecoregion (presence > 0)
species_sets <- apply(upset_df, 2, function(x) {
  rownames(upset_df)[x > 0]
}) |>
  as.list()

# UpSet plot for the same
UpSetR::upset(
  fromList(species_sets),
  nsets = 11,
  nintersects = 77,
  order.by = "freq",
  matrix.color = "#CC4945",
  main.bar.color = "#F78E1E",
  sets.bar.color = "#1EC2A0",
  shade.color = "#f1f1f1",
  matrix.dot.alpha = 0.7,
  point.size = 3,
  line.size = 1.1,
  text.scale = 2.0,
  mainbar.y.label = "BIN overlaps",
  sets.x.label = "BINs",
  empty.intersections = "off"
)

4. Optional: chord diagram for continental overlap

Code 
# -----------------------------------
# Generate pairwise overlap table
# -----------------------------------

# Convert to presence/absence
presence_df <- upset_df %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ ifelse(.x > 0, 1, 0)
    )
  )

cont_cols <- colnames(presence_df)

chord_data <- combn(
  cont_cols,
  2,
  simplify = FALSE
) %>%
  map_dfr(
    ~ {
      tibble(
        from = .x[1],
        to = .x[2],
        value = sum(
          presence_df[[.x[1]]] == 1 &
            presence_df[[.x[2]]] == 1
        )
      )
    }
  ) %>%
  filter(value > 0)

# -----------------------------------
# Dynamic colour palette
# -----------------------------------

grid_colors <- setNames(
  grDevices::hcl.colors(
    length(cont_cols),
    palette = "Dark 3"
  ),
  cont_cols
)

# -----------------------------------
# Chord diagram
# -----------------------------------

# Increase space between sectors
circos.par(
  gap.after = rep(5, length(cont_cols))
)

circos.clear()

chordDiagram(
  chord_data,
  grid.col = grid_colors,
  transparency = 0.35,
  annotationTrack = "grid",
  preAllocateTracks = 1
)

# -----------------------------------
# Add sector labels
# -----------------------------------

circos.trackPlotRegion(
  track.index = 1,
  panel.fun = function(x, y) {
    circos.text(
      CELL_META$xcenter,
      CELL_META$ylim[1] + mm_y(3),
      CELL_META$sector.index,
      facing = "clockwise",
      niceFacing = TRUE,
      adj = c(0, 0.5),
      cex = 0.8
    )
  },
  bg.border = NA
)
Code 
circos.clear()

5. iNEXT species accumulation curves

Code 
# Generate the occurrences data
occurrence_data <- bold_data_search %>%
  head(1000) %>%
  filter(!is.na(bin_uri)) %>%
  select(sampleid, bin_uri) %>%
  distinct(., .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  collect() %>%
  count(bin_uri) %>%
  pull(n)

# Overall species richness estimate (double sample size and true estimate)

# Pivot to wide format (species as columns)

inext_result <- iNEXT(occurrence_data, datatype = "abundance")

# Plot rarefaction/extrapolation curves

inext_plot <- ggiNEXT(inext_result, se = TRUE, type = 1, color.var = "Order.q") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("orangered")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(colour = "#011826", hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Number of records", y = "Estimated BIN Richness")
